full_text_en:
Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company v. Japan Nissin Container Transport Company — Dispute over Damages for Infringement of Pre-dated Bill of Lading (Appeal)

Appellant (Original Defendant): Japan Nissin Container Transport Company.
Legal Representative: Miyamoto Kei, Chairman.
Agent ad litem: Moriyama Saburo, Head of External Affairs Department, Nissin Container Transport Company.
Agent ad litem: Wei Youhong, Lawyer, Shanghai Fourth Law Firm.

Appellee (Original Plaintiff): Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company.
Legal Representative: Jin Hui, Manager.
Agent ad litem: Li Weimin and Guo Guoding, Lawyers, Fujian Dongfang Law Firm.

Original Third Party: Fujian Fu'an County Enterprise Supply and Marketing Company.
Legal Representative: Wang Tansheng, Manager.
Agent ad litem: Lin Wenqing, Lawyer, Fujian Fu'an County Second Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Shang Weixing, Lawyer, Shanghai Hongkou District Second Law Firm.

The Appellant, Japan Nissin Container Transport Company, being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (86) Hu Hai Fa Shang Zi No. 13 rendered by the Shanghai Maritime Court of the People's Republic of China on October 24, 1988, in the case concerning a dispute over damages for infringement of a pre-dated bill of lading initiated by the Appellee, Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company, appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court. The court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and, after public hearing, ascertained the following:

On March 29, 1985, the Appellee, Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company, as the buyer, through Fujian Fuxing Industrial Import and Export Company, entered into a sales contract with Japan Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. for the import of 3,000 Japanese Toshiba brand RAC-30JE type window-mounted air conditioners. The contract stipulated: price terms were cost and freight, port of destination was Fuzhou, total amount was 169,500,000 Japanese yen; the seller was to deliver 1,500 units before June 30, 1985, and another 1,500 units before July 30, 1985; payment terms were that the buyer, within 30 days before the loading of the goods, upon receipt of the seller's telegraphed notification of the export license number and shipment, would establish an irrevocable sight letter of credit in favor of the seller through the Fuzhou Branch of the Bank of China. The seller could negotiate payment with the issuing bank against the various documents stipulated in the contract, in accordance with the letter of credit terms, with the validity of the letter of credit extended to 15 days after shipment. The payment documents included a shipped on board bill of lading, blank endorsed, to order, clean and without defects.

Pursuant to the above contract, Japan Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. arranged for carriage with the Appellant. On June 30, 1985, the Appellant issued Combined Transport Bill of Lading No. WO15CO90 to the shipper, Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. The 1,496 air conditioners under this bill of lading were loaded on board the vessel at Yokohama Port, Japan, on July 1, 1985. After receipt, the Appellee sold these goods together with the 4 sample units received earlier.

On July 22 and 23, 1985, the Appellant received 1,500 air conditioners consigned by Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. at the container yard at Daikoku Pier, Yokohama, Japan. After completing container sealing and customs clearance procedures, the Appellant issued Combined Transport Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 to the shipper on July 25, 1985, in Tokyo, Japan. This bill of lading stated the carrier as Nissin Container Transport Company, the carrying vessel as the "Dacangshan" owned by Fujian Shipping Company, the port of loading as the container yard at Yokohama, Japan, and the port of destination as the container yard at Fuzhou, China. In the "Place and Date of Issue" column of the bill of lading, the Appellant entered "Tokyo, Japan, July 25, 1985", and in the "This is shipped on board B/L when validated" column, it entered "July 25, 1985". On August 20, 1985, the vessel "Dacangshan" loaded the goods under Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 at Daikoku Pier, Yokohama, Japan, and on the following day, the agent of Fujian Shipping Company in Japan, Hitachi Logistics Co., Ltd., issued an ocean bill of lading. The vessel arrived in Fuzhou on August 28, 1985.

Before the shipment of the second batch of air conditioners, the Appellee raised objections regarding the received samples, which could only cool but not heat, and repeatedly requested Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. to stop importing the second batch of 1,500 air conditioners, but this was not accepted. On July 27, 1985, Fujian Fuxing Industrial Import and Export Company received a telex notice from Japan Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. stating that the 1,500 air conditioners under Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 had been shipped on board the "Dacangshan" on July 25, 1985. After learning this, the Appellee, on July 29, 1985, entered into a sales contract with the Original Third Party, Fujian Fu'an County Enterprise Supply and Marketing Company, selling the 1,500 air conditioners under Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 at a price of RMB 2,000 per unit to the Original Third Party. The contract stipulated delivery by August 20, 1985; in case of delayed delivery, the supplier was to pay a penalty of 20% of the total value of the undelivered portion, and the buyer had the right to rescind the contract. The Appellee failed to deliver on time as it did not receive the air conditioners. The Original Third Party then, on August 26, 1985, notified the Appellee of rescission of the contract and demanded payment of the penalty as contracted. Subsequently, the Appellee contacted dozens of domestic entities for the sale of this batch of goods, but due to the sluggish market, no transaction was concluded. To mitigate losses, the Appellee, on February 10, 1987, re-exported the goods to Hong Kong Winstone Audio Visual Company Limited on FOB Fuzhou terms at a price of HKD 1,700 per unit.

On March 17, 1986, the Appellee filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court, seeking an order for the Appellant to compensate for economic losses caused by the pre-dated bill of lading, including loss of payment and interest totaling 48,460,600 Japanese yen, a penalty of RMB 600,000 payable to the third party, loss of operating profit of RMB 750,000, lawyer's and accountant's consulting fees of RMB 17,000, and postage and travel expenses of RMB 50,000. On June 30, 1986, the Appellant filed a counterclaim in its defense, seeking compensation from the Appellee for container rental fees of USD 14,728 and handling charges of USD 576.

On November 20, 1987, the court of first instance, considering that the third party had a direct interest in the dispute between the plaintiff and defendant, notified the third party to participate in the proceedings.

After trial, the Shanghai Maritime Court held: In container transport, the carrier can only issue a received for shipment bill of lading at the container yard. The Defendant, Nissin Container Transport Company, issued a shipped on board bill of lading before the goods were loaded, which constituted an infringement against the Plaintiff, Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company, and it should bear the consequences arising therefrom. Meanwhile, since the third party did not receive the air conditioners within the contractual period and rescinded the contract in accordance with the contract terms, storage and custody costs had already been incurred for the goods. Therefore, the Defendant's counterclaim against the Plaintiff for compensation of container rental fees and handling charges due to the refusal to take delivery was unfounded. Accordingly, the court of first instance ordered the Defendant to compensate the Plaintiff for the loss of payment for the goods under Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 and the advance expenses for re-export totaling JPY 39,723,200, interest on the payment loss of RMB 340,401, the penalty and interest payable by the Plaintiff to the third party of RMB 158,550, and loss of operating profit of JPY 61,338,700; the Plaintiff's other claims were dismissed. The Defendant's counterclaim was rejected. The court costs for the main action of RMB 16,700.17 were to be borne by the Plaintiff (RMB 2,881) and the Defendant (RMB 13,819.17); other litigation costs of RMB 9,350 and counterclaim costs of USD 150 were to be borne by the Defendant.

The Appellant, Nissin Container Transport Company, appealed on January 6, 1989, stating: The losses incurred by the Appellee, Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company, due to disputes with Japan Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. over the air conditioner sales contract should not be transferred to the carrier; the bill of lading issued by the Appellant after receiving the goods was, according to international container transport practice and the customary practices of Japan and China for container receipt, a "received for shipment bill of lading"; the Appellant's entry of dates in two columns of the bill of lading did not render it a "shipped on board bill of lading"; only after actual loading and the Appellant's fulfillment of its duties as carrier for shipment did the bill become a "shipped on board bill of lading"; the Appellant could not be held liable for delays caused by force majeure or unforeseeable events such as typhoons and port congestion; the shipper's negotiation of payment with a received for shipment bill of lading resulting in the Appellee's loss of payment was unrelated to the Appellant; the Appellee's refusal to take delivery despite knowing the goods had arrived at the destination port was the Appellee's own fault, and thus the Appellee had no right to claim "loss of operating profit"; the Appellee's unauthorized price reduction for the goods was its own loss. The Appellee's losses lacked a causal link with the Appellant's conduct and should not be recovered from the Appellant. The Original Third Party had no independent claim in this case and did not assume any obligations by relying on any party, thus lacked standing; the party with an actual interest was the actual carrier, Fujian Shipping Company, which should bear joint liability. Additionally, the Appellant expressed dissatisfaction with the dismissal of its counterclaim.

The Appellee, Fujian Ningde Economic and Technical Cooperation Company, responded: The bill of lading No. WO15CO97 issued by the Appellant was a shipped on board bill of lading, constituting the tort of pre-dated bill of lading, and should compensate for all losses thereby caused to the Appellee.

The Original Third Party, Fujian Fu'an County Enterprise Supply and Marketing Company, responded: The court of first instance had already ruled on the liability for the inability to perform the contract between the Appellee and the Original Third Party, and thus the third party had an independent claim in accordance with the law.

Upon trial, the Shanghai High People's Court held: The civil legal relationship between the parties arose from a contract for the carriage of goods by sea. The nature of Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 issued by the Appellant, with reference to the provisions of Article 3, paragraph 7 of the "International Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules of Law relating to Bills of Lading, 1924" and noting the provisions of Articles 6 and 7 of the Japanese "International Carriage of Goods by Sea Act (1957)", should be confirmed as a shipped on board bill of lading. The bank's negotiation of payment based on this was consistent with the "Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits". The Appellant's issuance of a shipped on board bill of lading before the goods were loaded constituted the infringement of pre-dating the bill of lading. The result of this tort was in Fuzhou. Pursuant to Article 22 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation)" and Article 4, paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of Maritime Courts", the court of first instance had jurisdiction over this case. The loading of the goods on the "Dacangshan" was determined by the Appellant and the agent of Fujian Shipping Company in Japan, Hitachi Logistics Co., Ltd., and the Appellant did not issue Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 under instructions from the owner of the "Dacangshan" or its agent. Therefore, although the "Dacangshan" encountered typhoons and port congestion causing delays during its 12th and 13th voyages in 1985, these could not serve as justification for the Appellant's act of pre-dating the bill of lading. Accordingly, the Appellant's request to add Fujian Shipping Company as a third party in this case was rejected. After the Appellee's request to Sanming Trading Co., Ltd. to terminate the contract was denied and the Appellee learned that the Appellant had issued Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97, it entered into a contract with the Original Third Party. However, because the Appellant had issued the bill of lading over 20 days before the actual loading of the goods, the Appellee was unable to deliver to the Original Third Party within the agreed time, leading to the Original Third Party's rescission of the contract as agreed. Subsequently, after the selling season for air conditioners had passed and the domestic market was sluggish, the Appellee had no choice but to re-export the goods to Hong Kong Winstone Audio Visual Company Limited. Due to changes in market conditions at the time, the Appellee's re-export price not only failed to yield the profit expected from the contract with the Original Third Party but was also lower than the purchase price. The Appellant's act of pre-dating the bill of lading caused operational losses to the Appellee, including loss of foreseeable profits, loss resulting from the difference between import price and re-export price, and loss from the penalty paid to the Original Third Party. The Appellant should bear compensation liability for these. During the performance of the contract between the Appellee and Sanming Trading Co., Ltd., although one party once requested rescission, in the end both parties performed under the contract, and neither caused economic loss to the other. Thus, there was no factual basis for the claim that the Appellee transferred losses to the Appellant. Regarding the outcome of this litigation, Fujian Fu'an County Enterprise Supply and Marketing Company had a legal interest. The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 48 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation)", properly joined it as a third party in this case. However, in calculating the compensation for the Appellee's loss of payment, the court of first instance included both costs and advance expenses for the import of goods under Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97—specifically the import agency fee, port charges, bank charges for import, and container stripping fees totaling RMB 41,955.46—which constituted double counting and should be excluded. The profit from the transaction between the Appellee and the Original Third Party should be calculated in RMB at the contract price. The court of first instance's conversion into Japanese yen at the exchange rate on the date when the Appellee was to deliver the goods to the Original Third Party was improper and should be corrected. The court of first instance's failure to calculate interest on the Appellee's loss of profit was erroneous; interest should be calculated at the enterprise demand deposit rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China. Given that after the judgment of the court of first instance, the bank loan interest on the Appellee's loss of payment continued to accrue, the Appellant's compensation amount for this item should be correspondingly increased. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China", the Appellee was liable to pay a penalty to the Original Third Party. Since the Appellee's breach was caused by the Appellant's tort of pre-dating the bill of lading, the Appellant should bear compensation liability for the loss suffered by the Appellee due to paying the penalty to the Original Third Party. The subject matter of this case was a general product. According to the "Regulations on Contracts for Purchase and Sale of Industrial and Mineral Products", the penalty range for the contract between the Appellee and the Original Third Party should be between 1% and 5% of the total payment. The court of first instance's determination of 5% was too high and should be amended to 3% of the total payment; furthermore, after ordering payment of a penalty for a party's breach, the court of first instance's additional charging of interest on that penalty was improper. Additionally, the Appellant's act of pre-dating the bill of lading did not necessarily lead to long-term storage of containers. The Appellant's counterclaim for container rental fees was reasonable and should be upheld. As for the Appellant's counterclaim for handling charges, since no reasons or evidence were provided, it was not supported. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 38, paragraph 1, item 1 of the "Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China", Article 35, item 1 of the "Regulations on Contracts for Purchase and Sale of Industrial and Mineral Products", Article 149 and Article 151, paragraph 1, item (3) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation)", and with reference to international practice, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (86) Hu Hai Fa Shang Zi No. 13 of the Shanghai Maritime Court is set aside;
2. The Appellant shall compensate the Appellee for the loss of payment for the goods under Bill of Lading No. WO15CO97 in the amount of JPY 38,019,618.5;
3. The Appellant shall compensate the Appellee for the bank loan interest on the loss of payment in the amount of RMB 362,671.1;
4. The Appellee shall pay a penalty of RMB 90,000 to the Original Third Party;
5. The Appellant shall compensate the Appellee for the penalty payable to the Original Third Party in the amount of RMB 90,000;
6. The Appellant shall compensate the Appellee for loss of operating profit and interest thereon in the amount of RMB 810,538.36;
7. The Appellee shall pay the Appellant container rental fees of USD 14,728;

The abovementioned items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 shall be fulfilled by the Appellant and the Appellee within ten days from the day following receipt of this judgment. Late performance shall be dealt with according to the "Settlement Measures of the People's Bank of China".

8. The court costs for the main action in both first and second instances total RMB 13,555.5, of which RMB 10,166.63 shall be borne by the Appellant and RMB 3,388.87 by the Appellee; the counterclaim costs in both first and second instances total USD 320, of which USD 20 shall be borne by the Appellant and USD 300 by the Appellee; other litigation costs of RMB 6,000 shall be borne by the Appellant.
